app_documentation:
The Flower Delivery App is a comprehensive e-commerce platform designed to facilitate the browsing, purchasing, and delivery of fresh flowers to customers. The application serves as a complete end-to-end solution for flower retail, enabling customers to explore a curated catalog of flowers organized by categories, view detailed product information with high-quality imagery, and complete secure purchases with flexible delivery scheduling. Built on a modern technology stack utilizing React for the frontend, Node.js with Express for the backend API, and PostgreSQL for data persistence, the platform integrates third-party services including Stripe for payment processing and SendGrid for transactional email notifications.

The primary features of the application include an intuitive flower catalog browsing experience with category filtering and search capabilities, a robust shopping cart management system allowing customers to add multiple items and modify quantities before checkout, a streamlined order placement and checkout process with delivery address collection and secure payment processing, real-time order tracking with status updates from preparation through delivery, and an administrative inventory management system for maintaining product catalogs and stock levels. The application supports three distinct user roles: Customers who browse and purchase flowers, Admins who manage inventory and product offerings, and Delivery Drivers who fulfill and track deliveries.

Designed with a mobile-first approach, the application features a modern, elegant botanical aesthetic with a soft color palette anchored by primary pink (#E91E63) and secondary green (#8BC34A) colors. The user interface prioritizes visual product discovery through high-quality flower imagery, ample whitespace, and clear visual hierarchy. The platform is fully responsive across web and mobile devices with breakpoints optimized for phones, tablets, and desktop screens. Accessibility is a core consideration with WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, including proper contrast ratios, keyboard navigation support, screen reader compatibility, and semantic HTML structure.

The intended users span both business-to-consumer and business-to-business contexts. Primary customers include individuals purchasing flowers for personal occasions such as birthdays, anniversaries, sympathy, or home decoration, as well as corporate clients ordering flowers for events, office spaces, or client gifts. The administrative interface serves flower shop owners and inventory managers who need to maintain product catalogs, update pricing and availability, and monitor stock levels. Delivery drivers use the platform to receive delivery assignments, update order status, and communicate with customers during the fulfillment process. The application's architecture supports scalability with indexed database queries, efficient API design, and integration points for future enhancements such as subscription services, loyalty programs, and advanced analytics.

glossary.Flower Catalog: A comprehensive collection of available flower products organized by categories (such as Roses, Tulips, Orchids) with detailed information including images, descriptions, pricing, and stock availability. The catalog serves as the primary browsing interface for customers to discover and select products for purchase.
glossary.Shopping Cart: A temporary storage mechanism that holds selected flower products before checkout, allowing customers to add multiple items, modify quantities, apply promotional codes, and review their order total. Cart items persist across user sessions and are user-specific, stored in the cart database table.
glossary.Order Status: The current state of a customer's flower order within the fulfillment lifecycle, progressing through defined stages including Pending (order received), Processing (being prepared), Shipped (out for delivery), Delivered (successfully completed), or Cancelled (order terminated). Status updates trigger automated notifications to customers via email or SMS.
glossary.Delivery Driver: A user role within the application representing personnel responsible for fulfilling flower delivery orders. Delivery drivers receive order assignments through the deliveries table, update delivery status in real-time, and can communicate with customers regarding delivery details or issues.
glossary.Inventory Management: The administrative functionality that enables authorized users (Admins) to maintain the flower product catalog by adding new products, updating stock quantities, modifying pricing and descriptions, uploading product images, and activating or deactivating items based on seasonal availability or business needs.
glossary.Payment Processing: The secure transaction handling system integrated with Stripe API that manages customer payment information, processes credit card charges, handles payment authorization and capture, manages refunds if necessary, and maintains payment status records (Pending, Completed, Failed, Refunded) for each order in the database.
